Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move ahead with the procurement finalization, our security team has two quick asks about the Private/VPC option where HealthCorp will retain the customer-controlled storage:

1) Can you confirm that we can enforce a region-lock (US-only) for our tenant so data never leaves the designated region? We need wording/assurance we can rely on for our compliance pack.

2) If we request a complete purge (end-of-contract or on-demand), what evidence will Redwood provide that data was removed from the customer-owned storage and any ephemeral caches? We need an auditable artifact (timestamped) to show to auditors.

A short reply and any sample artifacts (or an example handback matrix) would be perfect. If this needs to go to engineering/security, can you loop them in?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Rishi (security/ops) and Marissa (customer ops) to provide the details and the example artifacts you asked for. High level answers while they weigh in:

- Yes: for Private/VPC deployments we support tenant-level regional binding. For HealthCorp we can scope the customer-controlled storage (and runtime routing) to US regions only; that is enforceable via the deployment config and network policies.

- Erasure evidence: we provide a multi-part handback packet after a purge event that includes a deletion ledger (timestamps, request origin), snapshot tombstone report, and an ops-runbook note with the job id. We can also provide a signed attestation for enterprise contracts.

Rishi — can you paste the standard timelines and the two small example artifacts (handback matrix + short SOC2 excerpt) Elena can share with auditors? Marissa — once we confirm, I'll send over the doc bundle and a suggested contract clause.

Hi all — quick technical note and sample artifacts below.

1) Region-lock mechanics (concise):
- Tenant allocation: when we provision a Private/VPC tenant we pin the storage mount and control-plane node group to a specific cloud region and restrict cross-region routing via our smart routing layer.
- Network controls: VPC peering and egress rules are enforced by the customer's VPC boundary and our deployment manifest; there are no cross-region replication jobs enabled unless explicitly configured.
- Evidence point: deployment manifest + routing policy show the region binding.

2) Erasure & evidence (concise timeline):
- Initiation (T0): customer requests purge (API + signed ticket).
- Sweep (T0 + 0-2 hours): immediate deletion job removes active data objects from the customer-controlled bucket/mount. Job emits object-level deletion events.
- KV/Cache purge (T0 + 0-6 hours): runtime KV caches and ephemeral caches flushed; we log cache eviction jobs.
- Snapshot tombstone phase (T0 + 24-72 hours): snapshots marked tombstone and tombstone cleanup is scheduled per retention. If HealthCorp requests accelerated tombstone purge, we run manual GC and provide signed confirmation.
- Final scrubbing (T0 + 7-30 days): depending on underlying cloud provider and on-prem constraints, final low-level wipe (secure overwrite or cryptographic key destruction) is executed. This step timing is in the handback matrix.

What we include in the handback packet (standard):
- Deletion ledger: CSV with timestamps, filenames/object IDs, job IDs, operator ID.
- Snapshot tombstone report: list of snapshots affected with tombstone timestamps.
- Cache flush log: runtime cache eviction events (keys/types, timestamps).
- Signed attestation: brief statement signed by Redwood engineering lead with job ids and timestamp.
- Optional: we can add a short screencap of the job run (ops console) if your auditors want UI evidence.

Attachments attached: redwood_vpc_handback_matrix.pdf (matrix of timelines and options), SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (excerpt relevant to data disposition).

If you have specific auditor format requirements (CSV schema, signature format), send an example and we'll match it.

-rishi
